# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share test.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T test.ld $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: no libgloss at all -- vplat_syscalls.c provides every stub newlib
# needs, so only -lc/-lgcc remain.
VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c
VPLAT_LIBS      := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share test.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T test.ld $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: the SAME vplat_hello.elf (no rebuild) runs on `--model fast`:
# QEMU's andes_ae350 services the UART2 stdio and the new andes_sim_control
# device at 0xe0080000 turns the guest's exit write into the QEMU process
# exit code. Also asserts a nonzero guest exit code propagates.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andes-sim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --model fast "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "fast: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Nonzero exit code must propagate (vplat_exit41.elf: main returns 41).
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_exit41.elf >/dev/null || fail "exit41 build failed"
timeout 60 "$BIN" run --model fast "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" \
  </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 41 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 41"

ok "F2 vplat_hello.elf on fast engine (UART stdio + SimControl exit codes)"

icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same flags/libs/linker as the marked V
# fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the csrwi 0x7C0 markers).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS \
	  -T test.ld $(RUNTIME_SRCS) rt_c_v_matmul.c $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: one ELF built against the vplat runtime (UART stdio +
# SimControl exit, NO libgloss_vh / semihosting) runs to completion on the
# cycle-accurate engine from reset: it prints via the modeled UART and
# terminates the simulation with exit code 0 via the SimControl write.
#
# This is the leg that is impossible with an -mvh build (vsim has no
# semihosting; see docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).

## Features

| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|
| F1 | vplat-runtime | done | newlib stubs over UART/SimControl/HTIF; `vplat_hello.elf` prints + exits 0 on `--model cycle` | tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c, tests/fixtures/Makefile, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh | - |
| F2 | qemu-sim-control | done | SimControl MMIO device in the QEMU fork at 0xe0080000 (exit codes, putchar, NEWLINE); same ELF prints + exits 0 on `--model fast` | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f2.sh | F1 |
| F3 | hybrid-same-elf | done | same ELF on `--model hybrid --trigger csr`: markers wrap printf, "hello" prints from the vsim leg via the modeled UART, window_cycles + PASS | tests/vplat/test_vplat_f3.sh (no driver change expected) | F1, F2 |
| F4 | qemu-htif | done | HTIF file-syscall dispatch in the QEMU device (open/read/write/...; pico_stat layout) so fopen/fwrite parity holds; `vplat_file.elf` passes on fast + cycle | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh | F2 |
| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |

## Notes

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
  on QEMU too.
- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.

- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

1	// Subprocess helpers for andes-sim.
2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.
7	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP
8	#define ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <string>
11	#include <vector>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	struct RunResult {
16	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
17	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
18	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
19	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
20	};
21	
22	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
23	// and stderr are redirected to /dev/null. If the child runs longer than
24	// timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
25	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms);
26	
27	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING this process's stdout and
28	// stderr (its output streams straight to the terminal) and stdin from
29	// /dev/null; chdir to `cwd` first if non-empty. No capture, no timeout. Returns
30	// the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was signalled, or -1 on spawn
31	// failure. Used by `build` to delegate to setup.sh / build_*.sh / make.
32	int run_inherit(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, const std::string& cwd);
33	
34	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
35	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
36	// `run --model fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
37	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
38	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
39	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
40	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
41	
42	}  // namespace andes_sim
43	
44	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_PROCESS_HPP

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
31	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
32	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
33	// appended to its argv. csr contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
34	// themselves).
35	struct LegTriggerArgs {
36	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
37	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
38	};
39	
40	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. csr -> empty. pc -> qemu
41	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. icount -> qemu
42	// `,icount=<qemu_icount>` / vsim `--hybrid-icount <vsim_icount>`. Roles other
43	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
44	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
45	//
46	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
47	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
48	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
49	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
50	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
51	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
52	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
53	                                std::string& err);
54	
55	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
56	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
57	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
58	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
59	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
60	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
61	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
62	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
63	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
64	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
65	
66	struct PlanOptions {
67	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
68	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
69	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
70	};
71	
72	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
73	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
74	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
75	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
76	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
77	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
78	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
79	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
80	
81	}  // namespace andes_sim
82	
83	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
84

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F4 contract: HTIF file syscalls behave identically on both engines. The
# SAME vplat_file.elf creates/writes/reads/removes a host file (served by
# vsim's sim_control HTIF table and by QEMU's andes_sim_control mirror),
# prints "file io ok" and exits 0. Run in a scratch cwd; the tmp file must
# be gone afterwards (remove() worked host-side).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_file.elf"
SIM="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
QEMU="$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not built: $SIM"
[ -x "$QEMU" ] || fail "qemu not built: $QEMU"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_file.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

run_leg() {  # LABEL CMD...
  local label="$1"; shift
  local wd out rc
  wd=$(mktemp -d)
  out=$( cd "$wd" && timeout 120 "$@" </dev/null 2>&1 ); rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q 'file io ok' \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: missing 'file io ok': $out"; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: exit code $rc != 0"; }
  [ ! -e "$wd/vplat_file_test.tmp" ] \
    || { rm -rf "$wd"; fail "$label: tmp file not removed"; }
  rm -rf "$wd"
  echo "[ok] $label: file io ok, clean exit, tmp removed"
}

run_leg cycle "$SIM" "$ELF"
run_leg fast "$QEMU" -machine andes_ae350 -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native -bios "$ELF"

ok "F4 vplat_file.elf HTIF file io parity (fast + cycle)"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T test.ld -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul

# vplat fixtures: same source runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. They link
# runtime/vplat_syscalls.c instead of -lgloss_vh: stdio goes out the
# ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through the SimControl device at
# 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's andes_ae350 and vsim model. No
# semihosting anywhere, so the Phase-2 "no syscalls on vsim" cliff
# disappears for these binaries.
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41

RUNTIME_DIR     := runtime
RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# V fixtures use the standard C runtime (RUNTIME_SRCS). V regfile transport
# is handled transparently inside vsim via the Debug Module Program Buffer
# (ResumeDriver/StateDrain), so no per-fixture transport TU is linked.
# -nodefaultlibs suppresses the toolchain's default -lc/-lgloss/-lgcc;
# we re-add them inside --start-group so -lgloss_vh's semihosting stubs
# resolve newlib's _write / _exit / _sbrk / ... before -lgloss (the
# proxy-kernel ecall variant) is even searched. Order matters:
# -lgloss_vh must precede the fallback -lgloss path.
RT_C_LIBS       := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
# vplat: no libgloss at all -- vplat_syscalls.c provides every stub newlib
# needs, so only -lc/-lgcc remain.
VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c
VPLAT_LIBS      := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
RT_C_CFLAGS     := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv. The crt0 already sets
# mstatus.VS to Initial, so V instructions don't trap.
RT_C_V_CFLAGS   := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles \
                   -nodefaultlibs -I$(RUNTIME_DIR) -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share test.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (test.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S test.ld
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S test.ld semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: compile+link via gcc (newlib pulled). crt0.S is
# passed FIRST so _start lands at the load address (0x00100000) -- ld
# preserves input order within the .text wildcard.
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same runtime as the C fixtures, different -march.
# Listed separately so changes to RT_C_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_V_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(RT_C_LIBS) -o $@

# vplat fixtures: the engine-portable runtime (see RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES).
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) test.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(RT_C_CFLAGS) -T test.ld \
	  $(VPLAT_RUNTIME_SRCS) $< $(VPLAT_LIBS) -o $@

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in

input.command:
cat > /tmp/patch_nb.py <<'PYEOF'
import json

P = 'docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb'
nb = json.load(open(P))
cells = nb['cells']

def lines(text):
    out = text.split('\n')
    return [l + '\n' for l in out[:-1]] + ([out[-1]] if out[-1] else [])

def md(text):
    return {'cell_type': 'markdown', 'metadata': {}, 'source': lines(text)}

def code(src, stdout):
    c = {'cell_type': 'code', 'execution_count': None, 'metadata': {},
         'source': lines(src), 'outputs': []}
    if stdout:
        c['outputs'] = [{'output_type': 'stream', 'name': 'stdout',
                         'text': lines(stdout)}]
    return c

cells[12] = md('''## 2. Build ONE program for every engine

`fast` runs an ELF on QEMU alone - a **transparent passthrough**: the program's
own input/output flows straight through and QEMU's exit code is propagated.

Historically you needed a different build per engine: QEMU wanted `-mvh`
(semihosting), which vsim cannot service. This repo now ships a portable
runtime - the **vplat runtime** (`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) -
that talks only to devices BOTH engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Device | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550 @ `0xf0300000`  | yes | yes |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000`   | yes | yes |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF command @ `0xe0080010` | yes | yes |

No semihosting and no "which engine am I on" probe (a hybrid run migrates the
process between engines mid-run, so any boot-time detection would go stale) -
one binary therefore runs on `fast`, on `cycle`, and across a `hybrid`
handoff.

The build: your C file plus the fixture runtime (`crt0.S`, `trap.S`,
`handler.c`, `vplat_syscalls.c`) and the `test.ld` linker script (load base
`0x00100000`, valid RAM on both engines), with `-nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs`
and plain `-lc -lgcc` (no `-lgloss_vh`). The `say_hello` function and the
`roi_end` label delimit the region section 4d will measure.''')

cells[13] = code('''%%bash
. ./config.env 2>/dev/null     # sets HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (also done by `source ./setup.sh`)
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "toolchain missing - run: source ./setup.sh"; exit 1; }

cat > hello.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>

__attribute__((noinline)) void say_hello(void)
{
  printf("hello\\n");
}

int main(void)
{
  say_hello();
  /* ROI end marker for hybrid --pc-end: the return point after the call. */
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl roi_end\\nroi_end:" ::: "memory");
  return 0;
}
EOF

# vplat runtime: UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io; no -mvh.
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \\
  -Itests/fixtures/runtime -Wall -T tests/fixtures/test.ld \\
  tests/fixtures/runtime/crt0.S tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S \\
  tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c \\
  hello.c -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group -o hello.elf

echo "built hello.elf:"; file hello.elf''',
'''built hello.elf:
hello.elf: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, UCB RISC-V, RVC, double-float ABI, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, not stripped''')

cells[14] = md('''On `fast` (pure QEMU) it prints `hello` and exits cleanly - QEMU services
the UART and the SimControl exit device:''')

cells[15] = code('!andes-sim run --model fast hello.elf', 'hello\n')

cells[16] = md('''## 3. The SAME binary on pure verilator (`cycle`) - no rebuild

`cycle` runs an ELF on a single verilator (vsim) engine **from reset**, in
RTL - cycle-accurate but slow, because it simulates the whole program at the
gate level. With the vplat build there is nothing to rebuild: the binary from
section 2 runs as-is.

This repo built several cycle-accurate engines, so `cycle` refuses to guess
and asks you to pick one with `--engine`:''')

cells[17] = code('!andes-sim run --model cycle hello.elf',
'''andes-sim run --model cycle: model cycle: multiple cycle-accurate engines; select one with --engine (have: vsim:ax45mpv_mp2, vsim:ax45mpv_premium, vsim:ax46mpv_advanced, vsim:ax66_makatau, vsim:d23)''')

cells[18] = md('''Name an engine and run the same `hello.elf`. It prints `hello` and **exits
0** - exactly the leg an `-mvh` (semihosting) build can never run (see
`docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md`):''')

cells[19] = code('!andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf',
'''[info] loading segment: addr=0x100000, memsz=36224, filesz=35400
[info] hart 0 reset vector: 0x100000

- hsim forwards `KANATA_FILE` (and optionally `OBJDUMP_FILE`) to
  `tests/e2e.sh`, which appends `--kanata FILE --kanata-roi`
  (and `--objdump FILE`) to vsim's argv.
- vsim's `--kanata-roi` flag defers the kanata enable until after
  `--resume-from-qemu` loads the input state and `enable_hybrid_handoff`
  scans the ELF, then derives a one-shot `LoopGate`:
  - `start_pc` = the resumed PC (where vsim first fetches user code)
  - `end_pc`   = `--hybrid-exit-pc` (pc mode) or the unique
    `csrwi 0x7C0,1` PC from CsrTrigger (csr mode)
  - `skip_iters=0`, `record_iters=1` (open on first fetch of start_pc,
    close on first retire of end_pc).

---

## 5. Running the full test suite

After any change to the simulator or plugin, run the suite:

```sh
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

`JOBS=8` is the practical cap on this 128-core host (vsim Verilator
processes are CPU-hungry; the default cap of 128 saturates the box and
times out). Logs go to `/tmp/e2e-<RAND>/`; failed-test logs are
streamed at the end.

Run a subset:

```sh
FILTER=rt_c_v JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh        # only V-related fixtures
MODE=csr     JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # skip the pc-mode iterations
JOBS=1                     bash scripts/run_e2e.sh  # sequential for debugging
LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs       bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

For a per-mode handoff on the GEMM workload, drive `./hsim run`
directly (`--mode csr|pc|icount|simpoint`); see Section 4 for the
mode-by-mode commands.

The e2e suite runs via `scripts/run_e2e.sh`, not CTest; the vsim submodule
registers only the hybrid-layer doctest unit tests (there is no
`switching-mode` CTest label).

---

## 6. Common failures and how to read them

| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC / wrong icount value.     |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |
| `cannot resolve ROI start/end '<x>'`                   | PC-mode boundary `<x>` is neither a `0x` address nor a defined symbol. Fix `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`), or use CSR mode. |
| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in vmatmul_kernel`          | `VSIM_ICOUNT`/`QEMU_ICOUNT` too small (count target lands before the kernel) or wrong fixture for icount mode. |
| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

---

new_section='''## 5. One binary on every engine (the vplat runtime)

Fixtures linked with `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting) can print only where a QEMU
intercepts the semihosting `ebreak` triple; vsim has no semihosting, which is
why the Phase-2 "no syscalls inside the ROI" rule exists. The **vplat
runtime** removes the per-engine build split: it is a newlib stub layer
(`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`) that talks only to devices both
engines model at the same addresses, so ONE ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff.

| Channel | Device | QEMU andes_ae350 | vsim |
|---------|--------|------------------|------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | UART2 16550, `THR` @ `0xf0300020`, `LSR` @ `0xf0300034` | `serial_mm_init` (serial0) | `src/platform/uart.hpp` |
| exit code        | SimControl @ `0xe0080000` (u32 < 256 = exit code)       | `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` | `src/platform/sim_control.hpp` |
| file io (fd > 2) | HTIF magicmem command @ `0xe0080010`                    | same device | same model |

Build (same line for every engine; no `-mvh`, no `-lgloss_vh`):

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc" \\
  -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \\
  -Itests/fixtures/runtime -Wall -T tests/fixtures/test.ld \\
  tests/fixtures/runtime/crt0.S tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S \\
  tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c \\
  your_prog.c -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group -o your_prog.elf
```

Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io). Per-feature smoke
tests live in `tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f4.sh`.

Notes:

- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
  stat writeback).
- **Do NOT compile the csr ROI markers into vplat binaries.** CSR `0x7C0` is
  MILMB on the Andes core; the exit marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) enables ILM at
  base 0 and shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run (the program dies in an
  illegal-instruction trap loop). Hybrid runs only survive it because the
  exit marker retires on vsim. Delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use
  `--trigger pc` instead (see `tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c`:
  `say_hello` / `vplat_roi_end`).
- A `printf` inside the measured window now works (the UART is modeled and
  its MMIO cost is real), but it still adds those UART cycles to the figure -
  keep measured kernels I/O-free when you care about clean numbers.
- `docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb` sections 2, 3 and 4d run the same
  `hello.elf` through all three models.

---

'''

vplat fixtures are exempt from the Phase-2 rule: their syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure). **MILMB warning:** never compile the raw csr markers (`csrwi 0x7C0, ...`) into a binary that runs standalone on QEMU -- CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on the Andes core and the exit marker (uimm=1) enables ILM at base 0, shadowing DRAM (illegal-instruction trap loop). Portable binaries delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use `--trigger pc`.

## Notes

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
  on QEMU too.
- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).

## Features

| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|
| F1 | vplat-runtime | done | newlib stubs over UART/SimControl/HTIF; `vplat_hello.elf` prints + exits 0 on `--model cycle` | tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c, tests/fixtures/Makefile, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh | - |
| F2 | qemu-sim-control | done | SimControl MMIO device in the QEMU fork at 0xe0080000 (exit codes, putchar, NEWLINE); same ELF prints + exits 0 on `--model fast` | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f2.sh | F1 |
| F3 | hybrid-same-elf | done | same ELF on `--model hybrid --trigger pc` (`--pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end`): "hello" prints from the vsim leg via the modeled UART, window_cycles + PASS | tests/vplat/test_vplat_f3.sh (no driver change expected) | F1, F2 |
| F4 | qemu-htif | done | HTIF file-syscall dispatch in the QEMU device (open/read/write/...; pico_stat layout) so fopen/fwrite parity holds; `vplat_file.elf` passes on fast + cycle | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh | F2 |
| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |

## Notes

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
  on QEMU too.
- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

content.text:
Done. One binary now runs on all three engines. Five commits on `code-review` (roadmap: `one_elf_three_engines.md`), all tests green:

```sh
gcc ... crt0.S trap.S handler.c vplat_syscalls.c hello.c -lc -lgcc -o hello.elf   # ONCE
andes-sim run --model fast  hello.elf                                   # hello, exit 0
andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium hello.elf     # hello, exit 0, 3657 cycles
andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start say_hello --pc-end roi_end ...
#   -> hello (printed from the measured vsim window), window_cycles 14637, PASS
```

**What was built**

- **F1 vplat runtime** (`tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`): newlib stubs over the device ABI both engines already share - UART2 16550 for stdio, SimControl `0xe0080000` for exit codes, HTIF magicmem for file I/O. No semihosting, no engine probe (impossible anyway: hybrid migrates the process mid-run). vsim needed zero changes.
- **F2 QEMU device** (`QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`): mirrors vsim's `sim_control.hpp` at the same address; guest exit writes become the QEMU process exit code (verified with exit-41 propagation on both engines).
- **F3 hybrid**: one driver fix - `run_plan` was discarding leg stdout, so guest output never reached the user. Now relayed; F6/F9 golden parity unchanged.
- **F4 HTIF in QEMU**: full file-syscall dispatch (`vplat_file.elf` does fopen/fwrite/fread/remove identically on both engines). Gotcha: QEMU splits 64-bit MMIO writes unless `impl.max_access_size = 8`.
- **F5 docs**: tutorial notebook sections 2/3/4d now tell the one-build story with real outputs; USER_GUIDE gained section 5; CLAUDE.md documents the vplat family.

**Two findings worth knowing**

1. **The csr ROI markers are not QEMU-safe.** CSR `0x7C0` is MILMB on the Andes core; the exit marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) enables ILM at base 0, shadowing DRAM - any marked fixture (e.g. `rt_c_hello.elf`) dies in a trap loop on `--model fast` today. Hybrid only survives because that marker retires on vsim. Portable binaries delimit the ROI with PC symbols and use `--trigger pc`.
2. **Pre-existing e2e hazard (not from this work):** `run_e2e.sh` defaults `VSIM_BIN` to the alphabetically first engine, now `sim_ax45mpv_mp2` (2-core), where hart 1's crt0 SKIPPED write kills the vsim leg - 17 C-fixture failures. With `VSIM_BIN=.../sim_ax45mpv_premium` the suite is 35/35. First seen 06-09, before any vplat commit; both findings are recorded in the roadmap file.

Fixing the selection would just be a workaround; I'll fix crt0 so the fixtures are engine-agnostic, then the default pick (and every other engine) works. TDD: failing test first.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F6 contract: single-hart fixtures are MULTICORE-ENGINE-SAFE. On an engine
# with more than one hart (sim_ax45mpv_mp2, which is also run_e2e.sh's
# default alphabetical VSIM_BIN pick), secondary harts must park, not
# terminate the simulation: crt0's old `mhartid != 0` path wrote SKIPPED
# (0x01234571) to SimControl ~100 cycles after reset, stopping the sim
# before hart 0 could drain (hybrid) or even print (standalone).
#
# Two probes on sim_ax45mpv_mp2:
#   1. one csr e2e handoff (rt_c_hello) through scripts/run_e2e.sh
#   2. vplat_hello.elf standalone (prints + exits 0)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

MP2="$ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_mp2"
[ -x "$MP2" ] || fail "mp2 engine not built: $MP2"
[ -x "$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not built"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_c_hello.elf vplat_hello.elf >/dev/null \
  || fail "fixture build failed"

# 1. one csr handoff on the 2-core engine via the e2e harness
VSIM_BIN="$MP2" FILTER='^rt_c_hello$' MODE=csr JOBS=1 \
  bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "e2e rt_c_hello[csr] failed on mp2 (secondary hart killed the sim?)"
echo "[ok] e2e rt_c_hello[csr] on sim_ax45mpv_mp2"

# 2. vplat_hello standalone on the 2-core engine
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$MP2" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "mp2 standalone: missing 'hello from vplat': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "mp2 standalone: exit code $RC != 0"
echo "[ok] vplat_hello.elf standalone on sim_ax45mpv_mp2"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul
  # CSR-less spin loop; used by `./hsim run --mode icount` and the BBV-emit
  # / SimPoint stages.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  csr|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in csr pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*csr.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p))
total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f))
total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s))
step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

+  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).

## Features

| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|
| F1 | vplat-runtime | done | newlib stubs over UART/SimControl/HTIF; `vplat_hello.elf` prints + exits 0 on `--model cycle` | tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c, tests/fixtures/Makefile, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh | - |
| F2 | qemu-sim-control | done | SimControl MMIO device in the QEMU fork at 0xe0080000 (exit codes, putchar, NEWLINE); same ELF prints + exits 0 on `--model fast` | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f2.sh | F1 |
| F3 | hybrid-same-elf | done | same ELF on `--model hybrid --trigger pc` (`--pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end`): "hello" prints from the vsim leg via the modeled UART, window_cycles + PASS | tests/vplat/test_vplat_f3.sh (no driver change expected) | F1, F2 |
| F4 | qemu-htif | done | HTIF file-syscall dispatch in the QEMU device (open/read/write/...; pico_stat layout) so fopen/fwrite parity holds; `vplat_file.elf` passes on fast + cycle | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh | F2 |
| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |

## Notes

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
  on QEMU too.
- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
- FINDING (e2e, pre-existing): `scripts/run_e2e.sh` defaults VSIM_BIN to the
  alphabetically FIRST `verilator/build/sim_*`, which since the 06-09 engine
  rebuild is `sim_ax45mpv_mp2` -- a 2-core config. On it every crt0-based C
  fixture fails: hart 1 runs crt0 from reset on the vsim leg, takes the
  `mhartid != 0` path, writes SKIPPED (0x01234571) to SimControl and stops
  the sim before hart 0's drain (expected exit 200, got 0). Not caused by
  this task (first seen 06-09 15:30, before any vplat commit). Workaround:
  `VSIM_BIN=$PWD/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium JOBS=8 bash
  scripts/run_e2e.sh` -> 35/35 pass.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

# one_elf_three_engines: compile once, run on fast / cycle / hybrid

Goal: a single RISC-V ELF whose system calls work on every engine, so the
tutorial's "build per engine" split disappears.

Design (the "vplat" device ABI): the binary talks only to devices that BOTH
engines model at the same addresses:

| Channel | Address | QEMU ae350 | vsim |
|---|---|---|---|
| stdio   | UART2 16550, THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034 | serial_hd(0) | uart.hpp -> host stdout |
| exit    | SimControl @0xe0080000 (code u32) | NEW device (F2) | sim_control.hpp |
| file io | HTIF magicmem cmd @0xe0080010 | NEW (F4, stretch) | sim_control.hpp 17 syscalls |

The guest runtime is one newlib stub layer (`vplat_syscalls.c`) replacing
`-lgloss_vh`; no semihosting, no engine detection (impossible anyway: hybrid
migrates the process mid-run).

## Features

| id | name | state | description | key files | deps |
|----|------|-------|-------------|-----------|------|
| F1 | vplat-runtime | done | newlib stubs over UART/SimControl/HTIF; `vplat_hello.elf` prints + exits 0 on `--model cycle` | tests/fixtures/runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c, tests/fixtures/Makefile, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh | - |
| F2 | qemu-sim-control | done | SimControl MMIO device in the QEMU fork at 0xe0080000 (exit codes, putchar, NEWLINE); same ELF prints + exits 0 on `--model fast` | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f2.sh | F1 |
| F3 | hybrid-same-elf | done | same ELF on `--model hybrid --trigger pc` (`--pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end`): "hello" prints from the vsim leg via the modeled UART, window_cycles + PASS | tests/vplat/test_vplat_f3.sh (no driver change expected) | F1, F2 |
| F4 | qemu-htif | done | HTIF file-syscall dispatch in the QEMU device (open/read/write/...; pico_stat layout) so fopen/fwrite parity holds; `vplat_file.elf` passes on fast + cycle | QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c, tests/fixtures/vplat_file.c, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f4.sh | F2 |
| F5 | docs | done | USER_GUIDE section + tutorial notebook: one build cell, three run cells | docs/USER_GUIDE.md, docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb | F1-F3 |
| F6 | e2e-default-engine | done | `run_e2e.sh` defaults VSIM_BIN to the canonical single-hart `sim_ax45mpv_premium` (hsim's pinned default) instead of alphabetically-first `sim_*`; suite 35/35 with no env override | scripts/run_e2e.sh, tests/vplat/test_vplat_f6.sh | - |

## Notes

- vsim needs zero changes: UART, SimControl exit, and HTIF already exist
  (verilator/src/platform/{uart,sim_control}.hpp).
- The driver needs zero changes: `fast` already propagates QEMU's exit code,
  `cycle` already returns `sim.run()` (sim_control exits), `hybrid` already
  handles csr markers.
- Exit-code map (mirrors vsim sim_control.hpp): 0x01234567 FINISHED/0x01234568
  PASSED/0x01234571 SKIPPED -> 0; 0x01234569 FAILED/0x01234570 WARNING -> 1;
  raw < 256 -> that code. crt0.S's secondary-hart SKIPPED write becomes legal
  on QEMU too.
- HTIF needs the demo's dcache flush before each command (SimControl reads RAM
  behind the cache); harmless on QEMU.
- FINDING (e2e, pre-existing): `scripts/run_e2e.sh` defaults VSIM_BIN to the
  alphabetically FIRST `verilator/build/sim_*`, which since the 06-09 engine
  rebuild is `sim_ax45mpv_mp2` -- a 2-core config. On it every crt0-based C
  fixture fails: hart 1 runs crt0 from reset on the vsim leg, takes the
  `mhartid != 0` path, writes SKIPPED (0x01234571) to SimControl and stops
  the sim before hart 0's drain (expected exit 200, got 0). Not caused by
  this task (first seen 06-09 15:30, before any vplat commit). Workaround:
  `VSIM_BIN=$PWD/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium JOBS=8 bash
  scripts/run_e2e.sh` -> 35/35 pass.
- FINDING (F2): the csr markers are NOT engine-portable. CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB
  on the Andes core; the EXIT marker (`csrwi 0x7C0, 1`) sets ILM-enable with
  base 0, which shadows DRAM on a standalone QEMU run -> instruction fetches
  read zeroed ILM -> illegal-instruction trap loop (rt_c_hello.elf reproduces
  this on `--model fast` today). Hybrid runs are safe only because the exit
  marker retires on vsim, where the drain fires at retire. Portable binaries
  therefore delimit the ROI by PC symbols (say_hello / vplat_roi_end), and the
  hybrid leg uses `--trigger pc`.

   - Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional) + vsim (SystemC/Verilator, cycle-accurate), 2-phase handoff (QEMU1 drain → vsim resume+drain), no QEMU2 leg; cycle figure = vsim mcycle delta.

   - HTIF syscall numbers 5-22: gettimeofday=5, open=6, write=7, getcwd=8, lseek=9, read=10, flen=11, close=12, access=13, faccessat=14, fstat=15, fstatat=16, link=17, lstat=18, stat=19, openat=20, rename=21, unlink=22 (mirror of verilator/src/htif/sys_call.hpp).

The csr ROI exit marker `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` enables ILM at base 0, shadowing DRAM on standalone QEMU → illegal-instruction trap loop (mcause=2, mtval=0). Hybrid is safe only because the exit marker retires on vsim. Portable binaries delimit ROI with PC symbols + `--trigger pc`.
